title: ZKFold Symbolic: a Zero-Knowledge Smart Contract Language

ms.promise:
Context: zkFold Symbolic is a zero-knowledge smart contract language written in Haskell. It has a mathematical primitive called arithmetic circuits as its target. To create a zero-knowledge smart contract language, we must implement a compilation algorithm for every type or function that one needs to create Cardano smart contracts. We start with more basic types and operations and proceed to more complex and Cardano-specific ones.
Task: Implement basic types (boolean, fixed-size integer, fixed-size bytestring, fixed-size arrays) and basic operations with them. Implement equality, comparison, branching operations. Implement hashing functions.
Outputs:
・Modules for basic types and their opertations (Haskell)
・Modules for equality and comparison checks (Haskell)
・Implementation of branching computations (Haskell)
・Implementation of SHA2 and MiMC hash functions (Haskell)
ms.criteria:
・Modules for basic types and their operations can be found in our repo
・Modules for equality and comparison checks can be found in our repo
・Implementation of branching computations can be found in our repo
・Implementation of SHA2 and MiMC hash functions can be found in our repo

Context: zkFold Symbolic is a zero-knowledge smart contract language written in Haskell. It has a mathematical primitive called arithmetic circuits as its target. To create a zero-knowledge smart contract language, we must implement a compilation algorithm for every type or function that one needs to create Cardano smart contracts. We start with more basic types and operations and proceed to more complex and Cardano-specific ones.
Task: Implement variable-size types and operations with them (analogous to Integer and ByteString types in Haskell). Develop a set of examples, showcasing zkFold Symbolic smart contracts.
Outputs:
・Modules for Integer and ByteString (Haskell)
・A collection of 5 zkFold Symbolic smart contracts (Haskell)
ms.criteria:
・Modules for Integer and ByteString can be found in our repo
・A collection of 5 zkFold Symbolic smart contracts can be found in our repo
ms.report:
In this milestone we have finalized the implementation of the basic types available in the zkFold Symbolic framework, specifically unsigned integers and bytestrings. On top of that, we continue to expand our set of examples, having 5 of them completed at the time of writing.

Output 1 Modules for Integer and ByteString (Haskell)
We have compilation of the arithmetic operations, comparisons, and equality/inequality tests for the unsigned integer type into arithmetic circuits. The key parts of the code can be found here:
https://github.com/zkFold/zkfold-base/blob/main/symbolic-base/src/ZkFold/Symbolic/Data/UInt.hs
We have compilation of the bitwise and byte operations for the bytestring type into arithmetic circuits. The key parts of the code can be found here:
https://github.com/zkFold/zkfold-base/blob/main/symbolic-base/src/ZkFold/Symbolic/Data/ByteString.hs

Full documentation (instead of readme.md): https://docs.zkfold.io/symbolic/coding/getting-started/

Output 2 A collection of 5 zkFold Symbolic smart contracts (Haskell)
Here are the five smart contract examples that we have prepared:
・https://github.com/zkFold/zkfold-cardano/blob/main/src/ZkFold/Cardano/Examples/EqualityCheck.hs

This is an example smart contract where a UTxO or a token mint is blocked behind a secret number. The user who submits a transaction must prove the knowledge of a secret number in order to spend UTxO or mint a token.

・https://github.com/zkFold/zkfold-base/blob/main/symbolic-cardano/src/ZkFold/Symbolic/Cardano/Contracts/BatchTransfer.hs

This example shows how to create a "batch transfer" for the users of a smart contract based wallet. The users controlling the wallets sign their individual transfers. The data then gets aggregated to form a "batch transfer" transaction. 

・https://github.com/zkFold/zkfold-base/blob/main/symbolic-cardano/src/ZkFold/Symbolic/Cardano/Contracts/RandomOracle.hs

This is an example implementation of a random on-chain oracle. Users can supply their seed value
